Summarize Brown Heart Assistant..answer: Pranav designed and launched the Brown Heart Assistant (BHAI) as a full‑stack, citation‑grounded health‑education platform that now serves more than 5,000 users and is complemented by a searchable FAQ site [1]. The system uses a router‑orchestrated multi‑agent architecture that pulls information from FAQ, MASALA Study, Instagram, YouTube and movie‑timestamp agents, each employing source‑grounded prompts, confidence gating and medical‑safety refusals [1]. Retrieval is hybrid: BM25 and a pgvector HNSW index on Azure PostgreSQL are combined with NVIDIA embeddings and reciprocal‑rank‑fusion, then streamed through Azure OpenAI for chat generation [2]; query analysis, confidence thresholds and a human‑in‑the‑loop escalation tool trigger doctor‑specialty matching or appointment booking for low‑confidence medical queries [2]. A separate data‑pipeline enforces a manual review gate on the curated FAQ corpus, while a read‑only Astro FAQ dashboard is rebuilt daily from the production database and linked directly from assistant citations [3]. The production backend includes Azure Blob artifact hydration, checksum validation, signed sessions, per‑caller API keys and rate limits, LangSmith tracing across agent runs, and more than 420 passing tests to ensure reliability and hardening [2][3].

citations.title: Brown Heart Technical Stack
citations.snippet: For the Brown Heart Assistant, Pranav implemented hybrid retrieval using BM25, a pgvector HNSW index on Azure PostgreSQL, and NVIDIA embeddings/reranking, unified with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) and streamed via Azure OpenAI for chat generation. He built MCP-style human-in-the-loop (HITL) tool interfaces that trigger on low-confidence medical queries for doctor-specialty matching, clinician contact, or appointment booking. The production backend includes Azure Blob artifact hydration, checksum validation, signed sessions, admin health checks, environment-based model config, LangSmith tracing across agent runs and retrieval scores, and 420+ passing tests.

citations.title: Brown Heart: Data Review Gate, FAQ Dashboard, Service API
citations.snippet: Beyond the assistant itself, Pranav's Brown Heart work spans a separate data pipeline repo and a companion FAQ dashboard site. The data pipeline tracks exactly one file in git, the curated FAQ corpus, so every pipeline run produces a reviewable diff that must be checked before anything is published to the production Azure database - a manual review gate applying the same 'don't ship confidence you can't back up' principle to content curation that HITL escalation applies at query time. The FAQ dashboard (faq.thebrownheart.com) is a separate, read-only Astro site rebuilt daily from the same production database through a dedicated read-only Postgres role, and the assistant's FAQ citations deep-link directly to it. For non-browser integrations, a /service/chat API exposes the same chat contract behind per-caller API keys, per-caller rate limiting, and its own LangSmith trace tagging.

How does he approach RAG reliability?.answer: Pranav tackles RAG reliability by designing self‑correcting architectures that continuously verify and improve the retrieved evidence before an answer is generated. He combines hybrid retrieval—mixing dense vector stores (FAISS/Pinecone) with classic BM25 and Neo4j knowledge‑graph look‑ups—to broaden coverage, then runs multi‑step evidence‑sufficiency audits and bounded query refinements (including HyDE‑style expansion) to catch missing or low‑quality sources[1]. The system also applies confidence‑gating thresholds and medical‑safety refusal filters, ensuring that only sufficiently supported responses are returned and hallucinations are blocked[2]. These mechanisms together raise hit rates from 82 % to 92 % and improve faithfulness scores from 0.708 to 0.847[3].

citations.title: Agentic Graph-RAG: The Brain
citations.snippet: Pranav built 'Agentic Graph-RAG: The Brain', a self-correcting LangGraph agent that audits evidence sufficiency, expands searches to web/Wikipedia via Tavily when needed, verifies supporting snippets, and refines failed queries with HyDE query expansion before answering. It uses hybrid retrieval across FAISS/Pinecone dense vectors, BM25, and a 311K-node / 374K-edge Neo4j knowledge graph over 39K chunks, unified with NVIDIA and Cross-Encoder reranking. On 100 judged SQuAD-style examples it improved retrieval hit rate from 82% to 92% and LLM-judged faithfulness from 0.708 to 0.847.

citations.title: RAG Reliability & Audits
citations.snippet: Pranav approaches RAG reliability by building self-correcting architectures. In projects like Agentic Graph-RAG (The Brain) and Brown Heart Assistant, he ensures high reliability using query analysis, hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vector matching), Neo4j knowledge graphs, multi-step evidence sufficiency audits, confidence gating thresholds, and medical-safety refusal filters to prevent hallucinations.

citations.title: Case Study: Agentic Graph-RAG (The Brain)
citations.snippet: Pranav wrote a full case study on Agentic Graph-RAG: The Brain, covering the problem with naive RAG (generating fluent but unsupported answers when retrieval fails), the hybrid FAISS/Pinecone/BM25/Neo4j architecture, the self-correction loop with sufficiency auditing and bounded query refinement, and the results (82%→92% hit rate, 0.708→0.847 faithfulness).
